incident_title: GitHub broad latency after datastore major-version upgrade
first_minute_evidence: Issues, pull requests, notifications, Actions, repositories, API and login showed elevated latency and timeouts; unauthenticated traffic was hit hardest.
observed_symptoms: Broad slow queries and timeouts appeared across otherwise distinct services sharing upgraded data stores.
recent_change: Infrastructure for some data stores was upgraded to a new major version.
correct_first_branch: Check shared data-store saturation and resource contention introduced by the infrastructure upgrade; compare affected services by common datastore dependency and roll back the upgrade.
loss_created_by_wrong_branch: Source does not quantify diagnostic delay; service impact continued until rollback.
root_cause: Unexpected resource contention after a major-version datastore infrastructure upgrade caused slow queries and distributed timeouts.
review_notes: Correct branch is a curator inference from the source's shared-datastore diagnosis and rollback mitigation.

incident_title: Dependabot degraded after compute security policy blocked VM metadata
first_minute_evidence: Dependabot failed to create a portion of automated pull requests while VM create, delete and reimage operations failed in the underlying compute environment.
observed_symptoms: Automation backlog and failed VM lifecycle operations followed a telemetry loss and policy rollout.
recent_change: Security policies were applied to backend storage accounts after telemetry was lost.
correct_first_branch: Inspect the compute-provider control plane and recent security-policy changes affecting VM metadata access, rather than treating Dependabot itself as the primary failure domain.
loss_created_by_wrong_branch: The incident persisted until the policy changes were rolled back and compute capacity recovered.
root_cause: A loss of telemetry cascaded into security policies that blocked access to critical VM metadata, breaking VM lifecycle operations.
review_notes: The source identifies the dependency failure; the first-branch wording is curated.

incident_title: GitHub-wide degradation from user-settings cache rewrite storm
service_or_system: User-settings cache, background work and HTTPS Git proxy
first_minute_evidence: github.com, API, Actions, HTTPS Git operations and Copilot failed together while SSH Git operations remained healthy.
observed_symptoms: A broad multi-service outage spared SSH but affected HTTPS and services dependent on shared background infrastructure.
recent_change: A configuration change altered the user-settings caching mechanism.
correct_first_branch: Use the protocol asymmetry and shared service impact to inspect the user-settings cache rewrite path, background-work coordinator and HTTPS proxy connection exhaustion.
loss_created_by_wrong_branch: Two related degradation periods produced roughly 2 hours 43 minutes of customer impact.
root_cause: A cache configuration change triggered simultaneous rewrites that overwhelmed shared background infrastructure and exhausted connections in the HTTPS Git proxy.
review_notes: Protocol asymmetry is a strong early discriminator.

incident_title: Regional Codespaces provisioning failures after authorization-claim change
first_minute_evidence: Codespace create and resume failures spread progressively across Europe, Asia and Australia while US regions remained healthy.
observed_symptoms: Regional provisioning failure rates peaked near 90%; alerts fired but at insufficient severity.
recent_change: An authorization claim changed in a core networking dependency.
correct_first_branch: Inspect regionally rolled-out networking authorization claims and pool-provisioning dependencies; compare unaffected US regions against impacted regions.
loss_created_by_wrong_branch: Low-severity alerting delayed incident detection and response.
root_cause: An authorization-claim change in a core networking dependency caused Codespaces pool-provisioning failures.
review_notes: Regional contrast is the intended first diagnostic discriminator.

incident_title: Git LFS archive downloads failed after network misconfiguration
first_minute_evidence: Repository zip and tar downloads failed only when archives included Git LFS objects; standard archives were unaffected.
observed_symptoms: A narrow archive-download failure correlated exactly with the LFS execution path.
recent_change: An incorrect network configuration was deployed in the LFS service.
correct_first_branch: Branch immediately into the LFS-specific service path and its health-check/network configuration, not the generic repository archive pipeline.
loss_created_by_wrong_branch: Customer impact continued until the network setting was manually corrected.
root_cause: An incorrect LFS network configuration made health checks fail and caused an internal service to be marked unreachable.
review_notes: The LFS/non-LFS split makes this a high-quality branch-selection case.

incident_title: GitHub degradation repeated after high-volume user-settings cache writes
service_or_system: GitHub shared caching and dependent services
first_minute_evidence: github.com and API failure rates rose sharply; HTTP Git and Copilot degraded while SSH was comparatively unaffected.
observed_symptoms: The incident pattern resembled an earlier February outage involving user-settings caching.
recent_change: A large volume of writes reached the user-settings caching mechanism.
wrong_first_branch: Treating the event as an unrelated new multi-service outage instead of checking the known February cache-write failure mode.
correct_first_branch: Compare the signature against the February cache-rewrite incident and inspect user-settings write volume and shared cache infrastructure first.
loss_created_by_wrong_branch: The source identifies recurrence; exact diagnostic time lost is not disclosed.
root_cause: High-volume writes to the user-settings caching mechanism recreated the same underlying failure class as an earlier incident.
review_notes: Wrong branch is an operational counterfactual based on explicit recurrence, not a disclosed responder action.

incident_title: GitHub Actions queue degradation from Redis load-balancer misrouting
service_or_system: GitHub Actions background queue and Redis load balancer
first_minute_evidence: Most Actions workflows failed to start within five minutes, queue delays reached roughly 30 minutes, and some jobs returned infrastructure errors.
observed_symptoms: Job submission continued but processing stalled and backlog accumulated.
recent_change: Redis resiliency infrastructure updates introduced incorrect load-balancer configuration.
correct_first_branch: Inspect the Actions queue's Redis routing and recent load-balancer changes before debugging individual runners or workflow definitions.
loss_created_by_wrong_branch: The queue required additional recovery time after the misconfiguration was corrected.
root_cause: Incorrect Redis load-balancer configuration routed internal traffic to the wrong host.
review_notes: Queue-wide delay distinguishes control-plane routing from per-runner failures.

incident_title: GitHub-to-Teams notifications failed during upstream dependency outage
first_minute_evidence: GitHub event notifications to Teams failed with HTTP 500s and connection resets while unrelated GitHub services remained available.
observed_symptoms: Integration-specific failures affected delivery across many installations.
correct_first_branch: Check the Teams integration's upstream dependency health and connection-reset pattern before modifying GitHub event production or customer installation state.
loss_created_by_wrong_branch: Notifications were unavailable until the upstream incident was mitigated.
root_cause: An upstream dependency outage caused HTTP 500 errors and connection resets for the Teams integration.
review_notes: Useful dependency-boundary case.

incident_title: Audit-log datastore connectivity lost after credential rotation
first_minute_evidence: Audit-log history was unavailable through API and web UI; events were delayed but ultimately not lost.
observed_symptoms: The service could not reach its backing datastore immediately after a scheduled credential operation.
recent_change: A credential rotation failed.
correct_first_branch: Inspect secret-rotation state and datastore authentication before investigating event loss or application query logic.
loss_created_by_wrong_branch: Detection began six minutes after onset; event delivery was delayed up to 29 minutes.
root_cause: A failed credential rotation caused the audit-log service to lose connectivity to its backing datastore.
review_notes: Distinguishes access failure from data-loss failure.

incident_title: Copilot coding-agent sessions stalled under globally scoped rate limit
first_minute_evidence: New agent sessions queued for tens of minutes and failed in repeated waves after API request volume increased several-fold.
observed_symptoms: A single installation's traffic could exhaust capacity for all users, and rate-limited state persisted beyond the true window.
recent_change: A client update increased traffic to an internal endpoint by 3–4x.
correct_first_branch: Inspect rate-limit scope, shared credentials and cached rate-limit state before scaling workers or debugging agent execution itself.
loss_created_by_wrong_branch: About 22,700 workflow creations were delayed or failed during the incident.
root_cause: Rate limiting was incorrectly global rather than per installation, compounded by traffic growth and a cache bug that prolonged the limited state.
review_notes: Strong shared-quota diagnosis case.

incident_title: GitHub Pages failures from shared DNS resolver cascade
first_minute_evidence: Pages returned large volumes of HTTP 500s while services needing internal APIs, providers and storage failed together; cached lookups remained partly healthy.
observed_symptoms: Cross-service failures correlated with name resolution, with partial protection where DNS entries were already cached.
recent_change: A new traffic-balancing mechanism had been progressively rolled out.
correct_first_branch: Check internal DNS resolver health and the recently introduced traffic-balancing layer; use cache-hit versus cache-miss behavior to confirm.
loss_created_by_wrong_branch: An initial configuration rollback did not resolve the issue; resolver restart restored service.
root_cause: A traffic-balancing mechanism failed under a specific load pattern and caused DNS resolvers to fail.
review_notes: Rollback failure is a warning against anchoring on only the latest app configuration.

incident_title: GitHub search degraded when fronting load balancers saturated
first_minute_evidence: Issues, pull requests, projects, repositories, Actions, package registry and Dependabot searches timed out or errored together.
observed_symptoms: Different product surfaces failed only where they depended on shared search connectivity.
correct_first_branch: Map the failures to the common search dependency and inspect saturation in the load-balancing tier in front of search, not each consuming product.
loss_created_by_wrong_branch: Some search targets saw failure rates up to 65% during the peak window.
root_cause: The load-balancing tier in front of search infrastructure saturated, degrading connectivity.
review_notes: Shared-dependency mapping is the key first branch.

incident_title: GitHub disruption from online schema migration saturating DB connections
first_minute_evidence: Pull requests were most affected, while Issues, Actions, webhooks, Git operations and many dependent services showed latency and intermittent errors near traffic peak.
observed_symptoms: A broad service set degraded as normal traffic increased while a long-running migration continued.
recent_change: A routine online schema migration was running against a large heavily accessed table.
correct_first_branch: Inspect database connection capacity and long-running migration load; pause or throttle the migration before treating each affected product separately.
loss_created_by_wrong_branch: Customer impact lasted about an hour; the source does not disclose first-diagnosis delay.
root_cause: Combined load from the schema migration and peak production traffic saturated database connection capacity.
review_notes: High-value change-plus-peak-load case.

incident_title: Copilot code review failed after dependency release incompatibility
first_minute_evidence: Most requested code reviews returned a generic processing error while other GitHub functions remained available.
observed_symptoms: Failure began after a dependency release used by the review-processing workflow.
recent_change: A newly released dependency entered the processing path.
correct_first_branch: Check upstream dependency health and runtime compatibility before tuning Copilot prompts, repository permissions or review-request payloads.
loss_created_by_wrong_branch: Approximately 36,800 review requests failed.
root_cause: A newly released dependency was incompatible with the runtime environment.
review_notes: Separates model/application hypotheses from dependency runtime failure.

incident_title: Copilot frontier models disappeared after invalid configuration change
first_minute_evidence: Multiple frontier models disappeared from model pickers or returned model-not-available errors across web, editor and CLI; other models remained usable.
observed_symptoms: The same model subset failed consistently across clients.
recent_change: A production configuration change was applied and judged invalid by the system.
correct_first_branch: Inspect shared model-availability configuration and revert the recent change rather than debugging each client or inference request path.
loss_created_by_wrong_branch: Affected models were unavailable for roughly 54 minutes.
root_cause: An invalid production configuration change removed the affected models until the configuration was reverted.
review_notes: Cross-client consistency identifies the shared configuration layer.

incident_title: Background jobs delayed by hypervisor fault and connection storm
first_minute_evidence: Pull requests, pushes, Actions and webhooks accumulated delays up to several minutes while a background-job node timed out and repeatedly rebalanced.
observed_symptoms: An unhealthy node plus incoming traffic produced connection churn and continual rebalance behavior.
correct_first_branch: Inspect unhealthy queue nodes, connection churn and rebalance loops; remove the affected node before scaling every dependent service.
loss_created_by_wrong_branch: Delays peaked around seven minutes until the impacted node was replaced.
root_cause: Underlying hypervisor issues and a traffic spike caused timeouts, a connection storm and continual rebalances.
review_notes: Node removal is the source mitigation; first-branch phrasing is curated.

incident_title: Cloudflare BYOIP customer prefixes unintentionally withdrawn
first_minute_evidence: Only customers using Bring Your Own IP saw widespread timeouts and failed Internet connections; routes for their prefixes disappeared.
observed_symptoms: Applications were unreachable despite no evidence of attack, and impact was scoped to BYOIP prefixes.
recent_change: Cloudflare changed how the network managed IP addresses onboarded through the BYOIP pipeline.
correct_first_branch: Inspect BGP announcements and recent BYOIP onboarding-management changes before investigating customer origins or application health.
loss_created_by_wrong_branch: Affected customer services were unreachable until prefixes were restored.
root_cause: A network-management change unintentionally withdrew customer BYOIP prefixes via BGP.
review_notes: Attack is explicitly excluded by the source.

incident_title: 1.1.1.1 global resolver outage after prefixes were withdrawn
service_or_system: Cloudflare public DNS resolver and anycast routing
first_minute_evidence: UDP, TCP and DNS-over-TLS queries to 1.1.1.1 dropped globally while DNS-over-HTTPS using a different hostname/address path remained comparatively stable.
observed_symptoms: Resolver addresses became unreachable and their BGP advertisements were withdrawn worldwide.
recent_change: A service-topology refresh activated a dormant legacy configuration error.
wrong_first_branch: Treating a visible BGP-origin anomaly as the cause rather than checking Cloudflare's own route withdrawals.
correct_first_branch: Inspect anycast prefix advertisements and the latest service-topology refresh; compare affected resolver IP paths against unaffected DoH paths.
loss_created_by_wrong_branch: Resolver service was unavailable globally for 62 minutes.
root_cause: A legacy service-topology misconfiguration linked 1.1.1.1 prefixes to a non-production service, causing global route withdrawals during a later refresh.
review_notes: The source explicitly identifies an unrelated visible hijack that was not causal.

source_title: Post mortem on the Cloudflare Control Plane and Analytics Outage
incident_title: Cloudflare control plane failed after complete data-center power loss exposed hidden dependencies
service_or_system: Cloudflare control plane, analytics, Kafka and ClickHouse
first_minute_evidence: Customer configuration APIs, dashboard and analytics failed while the traffic-serving data plane largely continued operating.
observed_symptoms: Routers and systems in one facility went offline; supposedly highly available services failed because they depended on Kafka and ClickHouse hosted only there.
correct_first_branch: Treat data-plane health plus control-plane failure as a dependency-location problem; inspect facility reachability and non-redundant Kafka/ClickHouse dependencies.
loss_created_by_wrong_branch: Control-plane and analytics recovery extended across more than a day for some services.
root_cause: A catastrophic data-center power failure combined with hidden single-facility dependencies and incomplete full-facility failover testing.
review_notes: Vendor electrical root details remained partly uncertain; software dependency facts are explicit.

incident_title: Tiered Cache requests returned 530 after tracing code cleared routing headers
first_minute_evidence: HTTP 530 errors affected Tiered Cache, Images and Bandwidth Alliance requests, while content served from local cache remained healthy.
observed_symptoms: Failures spread with rollout and appeared DNS-related because origin hostname context was missing.
recent_change: Distributed tracing was added to Tiered Cache logic.
wrong_first_branch: Investigating an internal DNS release that was occurring at the same time.
correct_first_branch: Correlate 530s with Tiered Cache upper-tier traversal and the tracing rollout; inspect whether control headers and origin hostname context survive the hop.
loss_created_by_wrong_branch: Teams made several investigative attempts before confirming the faulty CDN release; peak impact reached about 5% of HTTP requests.
root_cause: Tracing integration cleared control headers needed by upper-tier requests, leaving internal DNS without the origin hostname and producing 530 errors.
review_notes: Source explicitly documents the misleading concurrent DNS release.

incident_title: Cloudflare traffic outage across busiest locations after network configuration change
service_or_system: Cloudflare backbone and data-center network configuration
first_minute_evidence: Traffic failed in 19 high-volume data centers while other locations continued operating normally.
observed_symptoms: Impact started immediately after a resilience-project configuration change in the busiest sites.
recent_change: A network configuration change was deployed to 19 data centers.
correct_first_branch: Inspect and revert the shared network configuration deployed to the exact impacted data-center cohort before treating the event as a global application failure.
loss_created_by_wrong_branch: The first center recovered about 31 minutes after onset and full recovery took roughly 75 minutes.
root_cause: A network configuration change made during a resilience project caused traffic loss in 19 data centers.
review_notes: Cohort correlation is the primary early signal.

source_title: Cloudflare Dashboard and API Outage on April 15, 2020
incident_title: Cloudflare dashboard/API outage after critical patch-panel cables were removed
first_minute_evidence: Dashboard and API connectivity failed after technicians retired hardware; diverse providers and facilities still shared one physical patch panel.
observed_symptoms: External connectivity disappeared and recovery was slowed by poor cable labeling and documentation.
recent_change: Technicians removed cables while retiring hardware.
correct_first_branch: Inspect the physical connectivity path and recent data-center work, especially shared patch panels and removed cables, before debugging application services.
loss_created_by_wrong_branch: Time was lost identifying which critical cables had to be restored.
root_cause: Critical external-connectivity cables were removed from a shared patch panel, exposing a physical single point of failure.
review_notes: Useful sociotechnical/physical-layer case.

source_title: Cloudflare outage caused by bad software deploy
incident_title: Global Cloudflare 502 outage from bad rule causing CPU saturation
first_minute_evidence: Cloudflare-proxied domains returned 502s globally at the same time edge CPU utilization spiked across the network.
observed_symptoms: The outage began immediately after a software deployment and ended after rollback.
recent_change: A bad software/rule deployment reached the global network.
wrong_first_branch: Treating the event as an external attack because of its global scale.
correct_first_branch: Correlate the CPU spike with the latest globally distributed rule/software deployment and roll it back immediately.
loss_created_by_wrong_branch: The global outage lasted roughly 30 minutes.
root_cause: A bad software deployment caused massive CPU utilization across the edge network.
review_notes: Source explicitly states the event was not an attack.

incident_title: Cloudflare disappeared from Internet after bad rule crashed edge routers
first_minute_evidence: DNS queries failed, pings and traceroutes returned no route to host, and edge routers across data centers crashed.
observed_symptoms: Packets could not find routes to the entire network; accessible routers crashed when processing the same rule.
recent_change: A bad network rule was present on edge routers.
correct_first_branch: Treat no-route symptoms as a routing-control-plane failure; inspect the common router rule and remove it before debugging DNS or proxy applications.
loss_created_by_wrong_branch: Physical reboots across globally distributed data centers extended restoration.
root_cause: A bad rule triggered system-wide edge-router crashes and route withdrawals.
review_notes: Clear distinction between DNS symptom and routing cause.

source_title: Post Mortem: What Yesterday's Network Outage Looked Like
incident_title: Cloudflare outage after DDoS mitigation rate limit was misapplied
first_minute_evidence: European network instability coincided with an upstream provider problem and active mitigation of a large DDoS.
observed_symptoms: Connectivity interruption followed a rate-limit action during an already degraded upstream-network condition.
recent_change: Operations applied a network rate limit to mitigate a DDoS.
wrong_first_branch: Attributing the entire outage to the upstream provider or to the DDoS alone.
correct_first_branch: Audit the just-applied mitigation rule and its scope while separately validating upstream reachability.
loss_created_by_wrong_branch: The combined failure made customer sites unreachable; exact diagnostic delay is not disclosed.
root_cause: An upstream network problem combined with a misapplied network rate limit during DDoS mitigation.
review_notes: Multi-causal case; source explicitly identifies both factors.

incident_title: Cloudflare network outage from routing-policy failure
first_minute_evidence: Approximately three quarters of Cloudflare traffic was disrupted across regions for up to about 15 minutes.
observed_symptoms: Large-scale reachability failure pointed to route announcements rather than application-level health.
correct_first_branch: Inspect BGP route announcements and shared router policy before application services or origin infrastructure.
loss_created_by_wrong_branch: A major portion of network traffic was unavailable during the incident.
root_cause: A routing configuration/policy problem disrupted Cloudflare route availability across much of the network.
review_notes: Public snippet provides less root-cause detail than newer cases; retain with medium confidence and re-review before production use.
